Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: every wrong submission costs 1 and every demo request costs 1. An
instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt cap is reached, and
reaching the cap is charged the full cap. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# Striped lattice with sparse markers

## When to Use
Use when regularly spaced solid separator lines divide a grid into blocks containing sparse exceptional-color cells, and output is a compact grid.

When a grid has regularly spaced full-color separator lines and sparse exceptional-color cells, the output may compact occupancy of the intervening blocks.

## Recurrent task-cede01c9: count-marker categorical lattice encoding (confirmed)

The grid is partitioned by full separator rows and columns into rectangular tiles. Each output cell summarizes the count of the sparse marker within that tile; colors distinguish count classes rather than mere occupancy.

Three demos establish the mappings by exact tile counts:
- Demo 1: 3x3 tiles, marker 7 in field 0 (separator 4). Tile counts were [[2,2,2],[2,2,2],[2,1,2]]. Output was [[1,1,1],[1,1,1],[1,0,1]]. Thus count 2 -> 1, count 1 -> field/background 0.
- Demo 2: 3x3 tiles, marker 7 in field 2 (separator 9). Counts [[2,1,2],[1,1,1],[1,1,1]]. Output [[1,2,1],[2,2,2],[2,2,2]]. Thus count 2 -> 1, count 1 -> field/background 2.
- Demo 3: 3x4 tiles, marker 7 in field 3 (separator 2). Counts [[1,2,2,2],[2,2,1,2],[2,2,2,1]]. Output [[3,1,1,1],[1,1,3,1],[1,1,1,3]]. Confirms count 1 -> field/background 3 and count 2 -> 1.

Solved test had marker 0 in field 7 (separator 4), 3x3 tiles. Counts were [[1,1,1],[1,2,1],[1,1,1]], so correct output [[7,7,7],[7,1,7],[7,7,7]]. Important: not binary occupancy, and output is not based on separator color. Derive actual marker counts tile-by-tile and use 1 for count 2, field color for count 1 (observed task counts in these examples were exactly 1 or 2). A first occupancy guess and subsequent attempts mapping count 1 to separator color / reversing class failed. Confirm count conventions with each demo before reuse.

## Confirmed task pattern: task-5fcb592f
Each logical output cell represents one block between full separator rows/columns. Output uses 1 if that block contains one or more sparse marker pixels, otherwise the sparse-field background color. Output is compact, not raw-coordinate geometry. Palette and separator spacing vary.

Evidence:
- 19x5 test, separators: full rows 4, 9, 14 and full column 2 (0-indexed). The four logical row bands each contain 4 rows; two column blocks flank separator. Sparse marker occupancy yielded evaluator-correct output 4x2:
  [[7,7],[7,1],[7,1],[7,7]].
- 19x11 demo: output 4x4, one marker at (1,3).
- 11x29 demo: separator row 5 and columns 5,11,17,23; output 2x5 with markers (0,0) and (0,4).
- 9x11 demo: separator row 4 and columns 2,5,8; output 2x4, rows [7,1,1,7] and [1,1,1,1].
- 14x19 demo: separator rows 4,9 and columns 4,9,14; output 3x4: [2,2,1,2], [2,2,2,2], [1,1,1,1].

## Confirmed task pattern: task-d715f5cf (current episode; test unresolved)
Across multiple demos (confirmed again in 2026-09), outputs preserve dimensions and recolor *all separator pixels* to 2: every cell on any uniform full separator row or full separator column is changed to 2, even if that cell was a foreign/noise color rather than the separator's base color. Other cells remain unchanged. Detect full monochrome rows/columns as whole axes; union them, then recolor every cell in that union. This is important: previous notes saying to replace only pixels matching the stripe's base color were contradicted by the successful test in which full rows/column were all 6, while stripe intersections and noisy cells on separator axes must uniformly become 2. The test had full rows 3,4,5,8,10 and full col 4; output recolored every cell on those axes to 2 and preserved all off-axis cells. Verify the axes carefully and do not recolor isolated same-color cells outside them.

Current episode demo axes:
- D1 23x26: full row 7,12,15 and columns 0,3,11 color8 ->2.
- D2 15x20: row4 and col5 color8 ->2.
- D3 24x7: rows1,4,7 and col3 color4 ->2.
- D4 23x21: rows10,14 and cols4,11 color0 ->2.
- D5 24x13: rows5,7 and cols0,8 color8 ->2.
- D6 19x28: rows15,17 and cols3,11,14,20,26 color9 ->2.
- D7 20x26: rows3,17 and cols0,8,14,16,24 color5 ->2.
- D8 28x13: rows3,5,8,11,12 and cols6,9 color0 ->2.

The test was 21x25 with full rows 4,13 and a full column 12, all color5. Eight submissions failed, including row-only and rows+column12 variants that seemed consistent with the demos. Therefore test solution remains unknown despite strong rule evidence; hand-authored serialization or overlooked axis likely caused the contradiction. On recurrence, input must be parsed into an array, detect complete uniform rows/columns programmatically, replace matching-color cells by 2, and verify all non-stripe cells are unchanged. Do not hand-copy or visually edit the grid; request demos if available and audit exact dimensions/coordinates before submitting.

This operation is separator recoloring, NOT compact occupancy. An older episode validated same rule on 19x7 and 28x9 grids (color7/3 stripes respectively), where every stripe pixel changed to 2.

## task-52f74e7a fresh recurrence, 28x24 test (2026-09-29): unresolved after 8 demos/8 wrong submissions

A new episode, distinct from all prior task-id recurrences, had 28x24 test. All eight demos and submissions were used, with no correct output. Demo output pairs (input dims -> exact compact output):
1) 23x29 -> [[2,3,3,3,3,4],[2,3,9,3,3,3],[3,3,9,3,2,2],[4,3,9,3,3,3],[3,3,9,9,9,3]]
2) 21x28 -> [[1,1,2,1,8],[8,1,1,1,8],[1,1,3,1,8]]
3) 26x22 -> [[6,6,6,6],[2,6,2,2],[2,2,2,0],[0,0,0,2],[0,2,2,2]]
4) 13x29 -> [[7,7,9,7,7],[0,7,7,7,1]]
5) 26x21 -> [[9,7,7,3],[7,7,7,7],[3,7,5,7],[7,7,7,7],[6,7,7,5]]
6) 30x19 -> [[2,5,6,6,6,6],[2,5,5,6,6,6],[5,5,5,5,5,6],[6,5,2,2,5,6],[5,5,2,2,5,5],[5,5,2,2,2,2]]
7) 29x21 -> [[1,8,8],[8,1,1],[1,1,4],[2,1,4],[1,1,1],[5,5,1]]
8) 27x16 -> [[7,6],[6,7],[7,7],[7,6]]

Test stripe marker rows (0-based) r=1,5,9,13,17,21,25 and marker columns c=3,7,11,15,19,23. Their values, in order by row:
[9,9,1,1,1,1], [9,9,1,1,1,1], [9,9,9,9,7,7], [9,9,9,9,7,7], [9,9,4,4,7,7], [2,2,4,4,2,2], [2,2,4,4,2,2].
Input background pattern alternates 6/8 in regular 3x3-ish tiles. The output mapping remains unknown: direct marker extraction, occupancy, and guessed compact reductions failed. Do not reuse any test submissions or claim a solved rule. Analyze all demos by exact coordinate mapping before attempting future recurrences.

## task-52f74e7a latest episode (2026-09-29)

See continual-arc-demo-inference reference task-52f74e7a episode for all eight demos and eight failed test outputs. No rule validated; do not reuse guesses. Test was 15x29, stripes rows 0,3,6,9,12 and cols 9,18,27, with 7/9 intersection markers, on 1/4 lattice. The observed compact outputs have inconsistent dimensions and no direct crossing-grid/crop rule established. Use coordinate-by-coordinate hypothesis testing across all demos before submitting.

## task-52f74e7a latest recurrence (2026-09-30): unresolved after 8 demos and 8 wrong submissions

Fresh instance; all eight demos and all eight test submissions were consumed without solving. Do not reuse prior task-ID episode rules. Test was 17x30, uniform tile fill 7, stripe color 8. Stripe rows r=0,3,6,9,12,15 and stripe columns c=0,5,10,15,20,25. The crossing matrix was `[[8,3,3,1,1,8],[8,3,3,1,1,8],[8,8,1,1,1,8],[8,8,1,1,1,8],[8,1,1,3,3,8],[8,1,1,3,3,8]]`.

The eight demo outputs, in order, were:
1. `[[4,4,4,0],[5,4,4,4],[4,4,4,4],[1,4,8,4],[1,4,8,4]]`
2. `[[9,9,0,0],[5,9,9,0],[5,9,9,9],[9,9,8,8]]`
3. `[[4,4,5,5],[6,4,4,4],[4,4,7,4]]`
4. `[[2],[6],[1],[1]]`
5. `[[5,3,8,8,8,8],[5,3,3,8,8,8],[5,5,3,8,8,8],[3,5,3,3,3,8]]`
6. `[[2,2,9,9,2],[2,2,2,2,2],[2,2,9,9,2],[2,9,9,9,9],[2,9,9,9,9],[9,9,9,2,2]]`
7. `[[3,3,5,3],[5,3,3,3],[5,3,3,5],[5,3,3,3],[3,5,3,3],[3,3,5,3]]`
8. `[[8,8],[8,4]]`

The output mapping is unresolved. Rejected hypotheses included direct copying/cropping of the crossing matrix, local 2x2 crossing rules, and tile-color fills. The last two rejected test grids were 5x5 `[[8,3,3,1,1],[8,7,7,1,7],[8,7,1,1,7],[7,7,7,7,7],[7,7,7,3,7]]` and 5x4 `[[7,7,7,7],[7,3,3,7],[7,3,1,7],[7,1,3,7],[7,7,7,7]]`. None is a solution. On recurrence, parse every demo's complete crossing matrix and compare output dimensions/content coordinate by coordinate before any submission; task IDs recur with new rules. This instance ended at cap, no accepted output.
This task has an elaborate 3x3-like lattice of separator stripes: demos 1–8 all produce compact outputs of varying dimensions (2x4 up to 6x5), but none established a reliable transformation. Demo marker colors occur only on full separating row/column intersections; output appears to encode some lattice-cell property, but simple occupancy, direct sparse-marker compaction, and guessed test outputs were not validated. Test 28x27 has horizontal full rows at 0,9,18,27 and vertical full columns 4,8,12,20,24 (separator color 6); 3x6 logical regions, with exceptional markers on separator intersections (top row 7s, middle row 0s, right side 9s; interior separator row includes 0s). Eight output guesses failed. If this task recurs, request demos (if available) and derive a coordinate mapping across all pairs; do not reuse prior guesses. Demos: outputs were 5x6, 2x4, 5x4, 3x2, 5x2, 5x5, 6x5, 5x4. Important task-8 demo input 30x30 had 5x4 output [[1,1,8,5],[8,8,8,8],[8,0,0,0],[0,8,8,8],[0,8,4,4]], demonstrating colored edge/intersection markers and compact lattice encoding, but no clear shared coordinate rule.

## Confirmed task-cede01c9 pattern (2026-09)
Inputs are tiled by full separator rows/columns into blocks; output has one cell per block. For each block, emit 1 if it contains one or more pixels of the sparse marker color; otherwise emit the field/background color (not 0 by default). Infer marker and field colors from the demo: demo1 used background 9 and marker 6, output 1 for occupied and 9 for empty. Demo2 used background 6 and marker 7, output 1 for occupied and 6 for empty. Separators in demos were color 2 and 9 respectively. For test task-cede01c9, separator color 2, field 4, marker 7. The 3x2 blocks produce accepted output [[1,1],[1,1],[1,4]]; the last block in bottom-right has no marker, hence 4. Count any marker presence; do not emit all-1 or infer output dimensions from number of colors. This occupancy rule is confirmed by both demos and accepted test.

## task-cede01c9 recurrence: stripe-lattice selector confirmed via demos + accepted test (2026-09-29)

A fresh instance had horizontal separators every six rows (input 23x14; rows 5,11,17) and vertical separator columns 4 and 9, separator color 3. This creates a 4x3 lattice of tiles (tile row spans 0-4,6-10,12-16,18-22; tile cols 0-3,5-8,10-13). Field/background 7, rare marker 8. One demo (17x15; horizontal separator rows 5,11; vertical columns 3,7,11, all color5) had 3x4 output; field6, marker9. Despite many marker pixels, output was 1 only for first-column tiles in first two tile rows; all other output cells were 6. The accepted test output was [[7,7,7],[7,7,1],[7,7,7],[7,1,7]].

Rule: output 1 only when a marker occurs in the rightmost column of a tile AND the tile contains the marker in a qualifying way: demo/test establish examples but not a fully clear generalized criterion. Coordinate audit: test row2 marker at (2,12) is in top-right block yet output there is 7; (4,8) in row1,col1 but output 7; (8,10) row1,col2 output 7; (9,6) row1,col1 output 7; (12,8) row2,col1 output 7; (15,10) row2,col2 output7; (18,7),(20,7) row3,col1 but output at row3,col1 is 1; and (22,12) bottom-right output7. Other test markers include (4,0),(7,0),(13,1),(22,0), all output7. Accepted output selected only (8,10)?? Recheck exact input/output alignment before reuse: output 1s are row1,col2 and row3,col1, while candidate marker coordinates are (8,10) in tile row1,col2 and (18,7),(20,7) in tile row3,col1. Thus selected tiles are precisely those containing at least one marker at the same within-tile row/column position as the demo's selected marker pattern, but demo detail is insufficient to generalize. Do not assume plain occupancy: it was explicitly contradicted by accepted output.

For the demo, output [[1,6,6,6],[1,6,6,6],[6,6,6,6]]; markers at (3,2),(3,6),(3,12),(4,0),(4,8),(6,12),(9,1),(9,2),(9,5),(10,10),(12,5),(13,2),(13,8),(15,13). Only first-column tiles in top two rows were selected, whereas other occupied tiles stayed field color. The accepted live test is authoritative; selector remains incompletely inferred. Avoid costly speculative submissions on recurrence; request demonstrations and coordinate-audit.

## Recurrence verification for task-cede01c9

### 2026-09-29 fresh instance: accepted test after 2 wrong attempts

Test 14x7 used separator rows 4 and 9 and separator column 3 (0-based), all color 5; field color 4, sparse marker color 7. The six logical blocks are 4x3, 4x3; 4x3, 4x3; and 4x3, 4x3. Accepted output was `[[4,1],[4,1],[4,4]]`: emit marker code 1 for a block containing at least one 7, otherwise field color 4. The four occupied blocks were top-right, middle-right, and bottom-left? Careful coordinate audit: test marker coordinates are (2,6),(3,0),(3,4),(5,6),(6,0),(8,4),(11,2),(12,4); corresponding logical block occupancy is top-left has (3,0), top-right has (2,6),(3,4); middle-left has (6,0), middle-right has (5,6),(8,4); bottom-left has (11,2), bottom-right has (12,4). However accepted output [[4,1],[4,1],[4,4]] indicates only columns are summarized by some distinct rule, not simple any-marker occupancy. Re-evaluation shows accepted grid shape 3x2; output col0 is 4 throughout and col1 is 1 in first two bands then 4 bottom. So only markers in right-hand tile of upper/middle bands count; markers in left blocks and bottom band are ignored. Earlier first occupancy-only answer [[1,1],[1,1],[1,1]] was wrong; second guess [[4,4],[4,1],[4,4]] was wrong; accepted answer [[4,1],[4,1],[4,4]]. Demo 1 was 14x7 with same stripe geometry (rows4,9, col3), background7, marker4, separator6, output [[1,7],[7,7],[7,7]]. Its sole output 1 at top-left corresponds marker at (0,2) within top-left block; other marker pixels at (0,0),(2,2),(2,4),(5,0),(12,0),(12,6) did not generate 1. Thus simple any-marker occupancy is contradicted by both demo and accepted test. The exact selection rule remains unknown; never reuse the generic occupancy hypothesis without more evidence. In particular this task instance's accepted output is authoritative for its test, but a future recurrence needs a new selector explanation.

**Caution:** This entry conflicts with earlier task-cede01c9 accepted recurrence notes in this skill that assert occupancy in every block. Treat each live demo/test as strongest evidence; task ID alone may recur with varying behavior or earlier notes may be erroneous. For this latest episode, strict block-any-marker rule failed.

A 15x8 test had full separator rows 3, 7, 11 and separator columns 2, 5 (0-indexed), all color 8. This yields 4 block rows x 3 block columns. Field/background was 4 and marker was 5. Accepted output was [[1,1,1],[1,1,1],[1,1,1],[4,1,1]]: emit 1 when a block contains any marker, otherwise field color 4. Bottom-left block was empty. A prior guess with 3x3 dimensions was wrong; always count separator intervals exactly and audit occupancy block by block.

## Workflow
1. Find full solid separator rows/columns before classifying sparse pixels.
2. Partition into logical rectangles; exclude separator lines.
3. For each block, mark whether any non-background, non-separator marker occurs.
4. Emit one output cell per block: marker code 1 when occupied, otherwise field background color.
5. Determine dimensions by counting logical block rows and columns, including edge blocks. Check that each demo's marker locations map to the output exactly.

## Pitfalls
- Do not emit original marker coordinates or preserve the input dimensions.
- Markers on separator lines are structural; do not count them as block occupancy.
- Output palette varies; infer the default value from demo outputs.
- Edge blocks can have different widths/heights due to cropping; still represent them as one logical cell when demos establish that convention.

# Repeat a sample panel across divider-separated regions

Use when a grid has a small patterned region and otherwise uniform panels separated by solid rows or columns.

## Confirmed Continual-ARC pattern: task-10dcbf72
A demo input 11x5 had a full vertical separator at column 2 (color 2) and full horizontal separators at rows 3 and 7. Its 2x2 upper-left tile was [[6,6],[8,1]]; output repeated that tile with period 2 throughout each non-separator cell, retaining dimensions and separators. The test input was 17x11 with full vertical separators at columns 3 and 7 (color 4), and horizontal separators at rows 5 and 11. The 3x3 top-left tile was [[1,1,1],[1,1,1],[1,1,7]]; a second panel fragment confirmed the 3x3 tile's lower-left cell is 9, making the tile [[1,1,7],[9,1,1],[1,7,1]]. Repeated this 3x3 motif with period 3 in both axes throughout all non-separator panels, preserving original separators and dimensions. Correct output confirmed.

Generalize: full-color separator lines partition panels, with a tile sampled/encoded in a panel; copy the motif periodically into each non-separator cell, preserving divider lines exactly. Demo: 11x5, col2 color2 and rows3,7 color2; tile [[6,6],[8,1]] repeated. Test: 17x11, cols3,7 color4 and rows5,11 color4; tile [[1,1,7],[9,1,1],[1,7,1]] repeated.

## Recurrence update: task-10dcbf72 (two demos; test accepted)

The task is periodic motif tiling in a grid partitioned by full-color separator lines. Preserve dimensions and separators; extend the pattern-bearing tile modulo the tile's period across the full grid, including all original/background pixels. Determine tile width/height and phase from demo.

This episode's demo 1: 2x7 input, background 1, solid vertical separator col3 color4; output adds at (r1,c5) color5, copying the non-divider pattern with period 4 horizontally (the motif region cols0-2 repeats at cols4-6 with the same phase). Demo 2: 8x29, bg2, separator columns9 and19 color8. Pattern-bearing tile has width9, period10 including divider; outputs repeat source motif at cols0-8 across cols10-18 and20-28, retaining divider cols9,19. The output repeats exactly each row's 10-cell segment starting at c0, including bg and special pixels.

Accepted test: 13x23, bg3; separator row6 all 8 and vertical separators c7,c15 color8. Source motif is upper-left panel rows0-5, cols0-6, with tile period 8 (7-cell content plus separator). Repeat upper-left 8x8 pattern block (rows0-5 plus row6 separator; cols0-6 plus col7 separator) periodically. This yields copied row pattern on lower panel rows7-12 (row phase modulo7) and copied columns8-14 and16-22 (column phase modulo8), preserving separator rows/cols exactly. The prior wrong attempt copied only sparse non-background markers inconsistently; accepted output copied the panel's background too, requiring exact periodic copy with local tile phase. Method: for each non-separator cell use source coordinate (r mod vertical-period, c mod horizontal-period) as supported by the motif origin; keep separators untouched. Validate full shape and all cell values.
## Workflow
1. Locate full uniform separator rows/columns and identify a motif tile.
2. Infer period and phase from sample dimensions; verify against existing motif fragments.
3. Fill regions by periodic copy, preserving separators exactly and retaining dimensions.
4. Check tile edges and ensure no divider is overwritten.

## Continual-ARC task-dc7bc826 — orthogonal bracketing fill, color 3 (confirmed)

For this task, process each row and column independently. If a line contains at least two marker-color cells, find the first and last marker; change every background cell strictly between them to color 3. Preserve marker cells and everything outside the bracket. Lines with fewer than two markers do not contribute. Apply both horizontal and vertical fills; intersections remain 3. Background and marker colors vary.

Confirmed by six demos:
- D1 7x8, bg4/mark2: row0 markers at c4,c7; output fills c5,c6 with 3.
- D2 26x4, bg2/mark7: row and column spans are filled, confirming vertical as well as horizontal bracketing; original non-background cells and markers are preserved.
- D3 8x16, bg7/mark2: row0 c0,c2 fills c1; other rows and columns with multiple markers fill internal background cells (e.g. c5 between rows5 and7). Confirms both axes.
- D4 11x13, bg8/mark7: row1 c4,c7 fills c5-6; row6 c3,c10-11 fills c4-9. Single-marker rows remain unchanged.
- D5 singleton-only input is unchanged.
- D6 isolated markers in 18x3 are unchanged.

A 23x27 test (bg6/mark7) was accepted with exactly this transformation. Implementation precaution: parse the exact input, mutate a copy, and serialize programmatically; validate dimensions and change only background cells strictly inside endpoint spans.

### Important recurrence caveat: same task ID, different unresolved rule
A fresh task-dc7bc826 episode with bg4/mark5 on a 20x11 grid disproved applying this generic rule blindly. Eight submitted outputs all failed, including three variants of horizontal+vertical bracket filling and identity. Seven demos: (1) 13x7 bg6/4 adds 3 at r2c3,r3c3,r4c3,r5c4,r6c3,c5,r7c3,c5,r8c1,c3,c5,r9c1,c3,c5,r10-11c5,r12c1-4; (2) 19x7 bg2/6 adds 3 to selective lanes/tracks (not universal bracketing); (3) 15x17 bg2/8 adds selective vertical/horizontal tracks; (4) 4x22 bg5/6 additions: r0 c3-14, r1 c1-2, r2 c1-2 and c8-17, r3 c3-7; (5) 29x22 bg6/2 adds 3 on selective tracks/regions; (6) 3x22 bg0/4 adds selected horizontal spans, not every possible interval; (7) 17x28 bg0/8 is identity despite two markers. The exact eligibility/selection rule is unresolved. Do not reuse universal orthogonal bracketing on recurrence without live evidence; compare changed and unchanged tracks, marker clusters, and local pattern constraints. This task episode capped at 8 wrong outputs, no accepted solution.

# Fill intervals between aligned markers

Use when an ARC demonstration shows sparse markers on a uniform background and adds a third color in spaces between aligned marks.

1. Identify the uniform background, marker color, and fill color from the examples. Keep all markers and all background cells outside qualifying intervals unchanged.
2. For each row, find the first and last marker. Replace only background cells strictly between them with the fill color. Do not extend past either endpoint.
3. Repeat for each column: find its first and last marker and fill only background cells strictly between those endpoints.
4. Preserve marker pixels even if a row/column interval crosses them. Overlapping row and column fills simply remain fill color.
5. Validate dimensions and allowed colors. Avoid extending rays to grid boundaries unless demonstrations explicitly show that behavior.

A key distinction: fill the intervals bracketed by markers, not every background cell, not just between adjacent marker pairs, and not unbounded rays.
